newsitem.title: PERU: Peru says refuses release of MRTA rebel prisoners.
newsitem.headline: Peru says refuses release of MRTA rebel prisoners.

text.p: The Peruvian government said Friday it refused to give in to demands by leftist guerrillas holding nearly 400 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence to release jailed comrades.

A Cabinet meeting of ministers agreed, "to approve the proposal of the President (Alberto Fujimori) not to accept the demand to release any terrorists held in Peru's jails," according to a statement read by a Government Palace official.

About 20 guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) have threatened to kill the hostages, including high-ranking diplomats, foreign businessmen and top government officials, if Peru does not release up to 500 of their imprisoned comrades.

At the three-hour meeting, which ended in the early hours Friday, the government also decided to "continue efforts, with an intergated focus on the problem, that would allow the prompt release of the hostages," the statement added.

Tentative negotiations with the rebels have produced no apparent progress although about 100 women and elderly have been released as well as four diplomats freed to mediate between the rebels and authorities outside.

Fujimori promised in a letter to U.S. President Bill Clinton that the safety of the hostages would be his first priority in resolving the siege. Fujimori met with Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda late Thursday to discuss options for ending the three-day standoff.
